papers.title: Muscle-inspired magnetic actuators that push, pull, crawl, and grasp
papers.abstract: Functional magnetic composites capable of large deformation, load bearing, and multifunctional motion are essential for next-generation adaptive soft robots. Here, we present muscle-inspired magnetic actuators (MMA), additively manufactured from a thermoplastic/permanent magnet polyurethane/Nd2Fe14B (TPU/MQP-S) composite using laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). By tuning the laser-energy scale between 1.0 and 3.0, both mechanical stiffness and magnetic response are precisely controlled: the tensile strength increases from 0.28 to 0.99 MPa while maintaining 30-45% elongation at break. This process enables the creation of 0.5 mm-thick flexural hinges, which reversibly bend and fold under moderate magnetic fields without damage. Two actuator types are reported showing the system versatility. The elongated actuator with self-weight of 1.57 g, magnetized in its contracted state, achieves linear contraction under a 500 mT field, lifting 50 g (32x its own weight) and sustaining performance over at least 50 cycles. Equipped with anisotropic frictional feet, it supports movement of a magnetic crawling robot that achieves up to 100% locomotion success on textured substrates. The expandable actuator exhibits reversible opening and closing under a 300 mT field, reliably grasping and releasing different objects, including soft berries and rigid 3D printed geometries. It can also anchor in a tube while holding suspended 50 g loads. This work demonstrates a LPBF-based strategy to program both stiffness and magnetization within a single material system, enabling remotely driven, reconfigurable, and fatigue-resistant soft actuators. The approach opens new possibilities for force controlled, multifunctional magnetic soft robots for adaptive gripping, locomotion, and minimally invasive manipulation of biomedical tools.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文虽不直接针对生物医学植入物，但通过LPBF工艺研究磁性复合材料的力学性能与疲劳行为，对AM力学性能研究方向具有方法学参考价值。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not study biomedical implants, osseointegration, or in-vivo/clinical validation; it focuses on soft robotic actuators with magnetic response.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过LPBF制备可编程刚度和磁响应的软体致动器
summary_zh.method: 采用激光粉末床熔融工艺加工热塑性聚氨酯/钕铁硼复合材料，调节激光能量控制性能
summary_zh.result: 致动器实现大变形、负载能力及50次循环稳定性，可爬行和抓取物体
summary_zh.validation: 拉伸测试和循环致动实验验证力学性能与耐久性

summary_en.motivation: To create functional magnetic composites with controlled stiffness and magnetization via additive manufacturing for soft robotic actuators.
summary_en.method: Laser powder bed fusion of a thermoplastic polyurethane/Nd2Fe14B composite with tunable laser energy to achieve desired mechanical and magnetic properties.
summary_en.result: Actuators demonstrate reversible bending, linear contraction lifting 32x self-weight, over 50 cycles, and successful locomotion and grasping tasks.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing (tensile strength, elongation) and cyclic actuation experiments confirm performance and fatigue resistance.
